data.gender_notes: Lindsey is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Old English Lindisfarne, meaning 'island of Lind' or 'cliff island'. The name has Anglo-Saxon roots and was popularized by Saint Lindisfarne, who brought Christianity to the Northumbrian islands. The name Lindsey carries the meaning “Island of Lind” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Lindsey usually hope their child will grow to embody island of lind and live with faith, good character and purpose.
